'''William Wesley Peterson''' (April 22, 1924 – May 6, 2009) was an American mathematician and computer scientist.  He was best known for designing the [[cyclic redundancy check]] (CRC),<ref name="PetersonBrown1961">{{cite journal| last1=Peterson |first1=W. W.  |last2=Brown |first2=D. T.| date=January 1961| title = Cyclic Codes for Error Detection| journal = Proceedings of the IRE| doi = 10.1109/JRPROC.1961.287814| volume = 49| pages = 228–235|s2cid=51666741}} – The original paper on CRCs</ref> for which research he was awarded the [[Japan Prize]] in 1999.<ref name="Peterson_JapanPrize">{{cite web|url=http://www.japanprize.jp/en/prize_prof_1999_peterson.html |title=Dr. W. Wesley Peterson, 1999 (15th) Japan Prize Laureate |publisher=Japan Prize Foundation |access-date=November 24, 2011}}</ref>

== Biography ==
Peterson was born on April 22, 1924, in [[Muskegon, Michigan]] and earned his [[Ph.D.]] in 1954 from the [[University of Michigan]].<ref name="Peterson_JapanPrize"/><ref name="Peterson_Obituary">{{cite web|url=http://the.honoluluadvertiser.com/article/2009/May/17/ln/hawaii905170366.html |title=Obituaries, Dr. William Wesley Peterson |publisher=[[The Honolulu Advertiser]] |date=May 17, 2009 |access-date=November 24, 2011}}</ref> Peterson was a professor of [[Information and Computer Science]]s at the [[University of Hawaii at Manoa]], joining the faculty in 1964.<ref name="KeKumuIke99">[http://www.artsci.hawaii.edu/alumni/Documents/KKI/KKIsummer1999_comp2.pdf The Newsletter of the Colleges of Arts & Sciences at the University of Hawaii at Manoa, Summer 1999, Volume 5, Number One] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120426001553/http://www.artsci.hawaii.edu/alumni/Documents/KKI/KKIsummer1999_comp2.pdf |date=April 26, 2012 }} Retrieved November 24, 2011</ref>  He started work at IBM in 1954.<ref name="KeKumuIke99" /> He authored the publication of algebraic coding theory ''Error Correcting Codes'' in 1961.  He co-authored a number of books on the topic of [[error correcting code]]s, including the revised 2nd edition of ''Error Correcting Codes''<ref name="PetersonWeldon1971">
{{cite book
| last1 = Peterson |first1=W. W.
| last2 = Weldon |first2=E. J.
| year = 1971
| title = Error Correcting Codes, Revised 2nd Edition
| publisher = MIT Press
| isbn = 0-262-16039-0
| url = https://archive.org/details/errorcorrectingc00pete
}}
</ref> (co-authored with [[Edward J. Weldon]]).  In the early 1950s, he contributed significantly to the development of [[Detection theory|signal detection theory]] through participation in the [[IRE Professional Group on Information Theory]].<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Peterson |first1=W. W.|last2=Birdsall |first2=T. G.| last3=Fox |first3=W. C. |year=1954|title= The theory of signal detectability|doi=10.1109/TIT.1954.1057460|journal= Transactions of the IRE Professional Group on Information Theory|volume=4|issue=4|pages= 171–212}}</ref> He has also done research and published in the fields of [[programming language]]s,<ref name="Peterson1974">
{{cite book
| author = Peterson |first1=W. W.
| date = June 1974
| title = Introduction to Programming Languages
| publisher = Prentice Hall College Div
| isbn = 978-0-13-493486-0
| url = https://archive.org/details/introductiontopr0000pete
}}
</ref> [[system programming|systems programming]], and [[computer networking|networks]].  As well as the [[Japan Prize]] in 1999,<ref name="Peterson_JapanPrize"/><ref name="JapanPrize_Star-Bulletin">{{cite web |url=http://archives.starbulletin.com/98/12/16/news/story6.html |title=W. Wesley Peterson receives Japan Prize for work in digital error control |author=Mary Adamski |publisher=[[Honolulu Star-Bulletin]] |date=December 16, 1998 |access-date=November 24, 2011}}</ref> he was awarded the [[Claude E. Shannon Award]] in 1981,<ref name="KeKumuIke99" /> and the [[IEEE Centennial Medal]] in 1984.<ref name="KeKumuIke99" /> In 2007, two years before Peterson's death, [[Intel]] added crc32 to the [[SSE4#SSE4.2|SSE4.2]] instruction set of the [[X86#x86-64|x86-64]] architecture.<ref>{{ cite web| url=https://software.intel.com/sites/default/files/m/8/b/8/D9156103.pdf | access-date=2023-11-30 | title=Intel® SSE4 Programming Reference | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151005015805/https://software.intel.com/sites/default/files/m/8/b/8/D9156103.pdf | archive-date=2015-10-05}}</ref>
 
Peterson finished 16th in the 2005 Honolulu Marathon for males ages 80 to 84.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://archives.starbulletin.com/2005/12/11/news/resultsdivisions.html |title=Honolulu Marathon Updates – Results by division – Males 80 to 84 |publisher=Honolulu Star-Bulletin |date=December 11, 2005 |access-date=November 24, 2011}}</ref> He died on May 6, 2009, in [[Honolulu, Hawaii]] survived by five children from two different marriages, his wife, and several grandchildren.<ref name="Peterson_Obituary"/>
